name: Trent Rojas
summary: A 47-year-old critical facilities engineer on Crew B who walks Hall B3's generators, cooling units and power gear on 12-hour days, and who has made more friends in two years at Vira than most people make in ten. He grew up in Bakersfield, worked boilers and chillers at a Victorville hospital for sixteen years, and lives on Yucca Street in Saltbrush with his wife Noor, who also works security at Vira, and their two kids.

backstory.childhood: Born February 8, 1979, in Bakersfield, California, the youngest of four boys, in a three-bedroom house on the east side that always smelled like his father's work boots. His father worked as a roustabout and later a pumper in the oil fields out by Taft. Trent spent summers riding along in the company truck, learning to read gauges before he could read chapter books. He was a decent shortstop, a bad student until shop class and a good kid mostly because his mother would have killed him otherwise.
backstory.family_of_origin: His father, Ray Rojas, 74, is retired with a bad back and a recliner that faces a television permanently tuned to Dodgers games. His mother, Gloria, 72, still plays piano at a Pentecostal church in Bakersfield every Sunday and prays for Trent by name in front of the congregation, which he finds both touching and humiliating. Three older brothers: Ray Jr. is a Kern County sheriff's deputy, Danny does drywall, and Mike died in a motorcycle crash in 2002, which the family doesn't talk about and Trent thinks about every time he sees a bike on the highway.
backstory.education: Bakersfield High, class of 1997, where the HVAC teacher, Mr. Ochoa, saved him. Two years in an HVAC and refrigeration program at Bakersfield College, then an apprenticeship. He holds a universal EPA refrigerant certification, a stationary engineer license from his hospital years, and a pile of vendor certifications on generator controls and chillers, framed in the garage because Noor won't have them in the living room.
backstory.before_vira: Commercial HVAC in Bakersfield from 1999 to 2005, mostly rooftop units on strip malls in July. In 2005 he took a plant operations job at a hospital in Victorville and stayed sixteen years, working boilers, chillers, medical gas, emergency generators and every leak in a sixty-year-old building. He loved it. He met Noor there in 2014 when she chained a stairwell door during a lockdown drill and he needed to get to a boiler. In 2021 the hospital outsourced plant operations, and the contractor offered him his own job back at fourteen percent less, so he quit. He spent 2022 to 2024 as a maintenance mechanic at the quarry in Ironwood, working on crushers, conveyors and the diesel gensets. The pay was fine, the dust was terrible, and the drive from Saltbrush was long.
backstory.how_they_came_to_vira: Noor had been at Vira almost two years and kept coming home talking about the generator yards. In the fall of 2024 she walked his resume into the HR office herself and handed it to Owen Bustamante. Owen called him the same week, and they talked for forty minutes, half of it about high school baseball. Hana Sato interviewed him on a Crew B day in the generator yard and asked him to diagnose a fake fault on a transfer switch, and he found it in four minutes. He started in December 2024.
turning_points: His brother Mike's death in 2002. Trent was 23, and he quit drinking for good about a year later, after one bad night that Gloria still doesn't know about.

The 2011 power failure at the Victorville hospital, when the second generator didn't pick up and he hand-transferred the ICU load in the dark with a flashlight in his teeth. People still tell that story at the hospital, and he never brings it up himself.
Meeting Noor, a divorced woman six years older with a six-year-old son, and knowing inside a month that this was it, which surprised his mother more than anyone.
Adopting Isaac in 2020 after Isaac asked him in the truck, out of nowhere, if he could be a Rojas. Trent had to pull over.
Quitting the hospital rather than taking the contractor's pay cut. It was the first time in his life he chose pride over safety, and it worked out, mostly because of Noor.

household_notes.note: Noor. Married ten years, together twelve. She works fixed 6-to-2 days on security and he works 12-hour Crew B days on the 2-2-3 rotation, so the house runs on the fridge whiteboard: her green, him blue, Isaac red, and Maya's horse drawings all over it. On the mornings they both work, they leave at 5:15 in two cars, and he flashes his brights at her once at the Vira turnoff, which started as a joke and is now a rule. On his workdays he gets home at 6:45 to a plate under foil and a wife already half asleep. On his three-day off stretches he does everything: school runs, dinners, the lawn, Maya's hair, badly. He knows she feels like the weekday parent and he's the weekend one. He hears it as a fair complaint and an unfair one at the same time, and he hasn't said that to her.

His son by adoption since 2020 and by every other measure since Isaac was seven. Isaac graduated in May and works at the hardware store in Saltbrush. He's paying off the 2009 Tacoma at forty dollars a week, and Trent quietly puts every payment into an account in Isaac's name. Trent is the one pushing lineman school, sending him videos and talking up the pay. He knows Noor thinks he's pushing because he's scared of the Navy too, and she's right.

Third grade, horse-obsessed, and convinced her father can fix anything, which he has not corrected. On his days off he makes pancakes shaped like states, and she has to guess them. She's gotten too good at it, so he's started doing counties. She recently began announcing which parent is 'home-home today,' and the first time she said it to him he laughed, and then he lay awake about it.

traits: a little vain about his memory
values: doing the job so nobody notices it was done
never letting the kids see him scared
fears: A failure on his rounds that he should have caught
Isaac ending up on a motorcycle
His marriage becoming a pair of schedules that pass in the driveway
Getting old the way his father did, in a chair, angry
personality.humor: Loud, physical and corny. He does voices, gives generators nicknames, and tells the same three jokes about Bakersfield on a loop. He's the one who puts a cake in the Crew B break room for every birthday, and he knows everyone's.
personality.temper: Very slow, and it comes out in one burst over safety: a lockout skipped, a panel left open, somebody in the generator yard without ear protection. At home he goes quiet instead, mows the lawn and comes back in an hour to apologize, whether or not it was his fault.
quirks: Names the generators in B3 after Dodgers infielders and talks to them by name on rounds
Taps every gauge glass twice, the way his father did
Always carries two pens and a pocket flashlight, and gives the pens away constantly
Can tell you the refrigerant charge of almost any chiller he's ever touched
Hums hymns from his mother's church without realizing it

voice.how_they_talk: Warm, quick and a little loud, with a Bakersfield drawl that gets thicker when he's tired or talking about baseball. He tells stories with his hands and loses the point, then finds it again. He calls almost every man 'brother' and almost every woman by her name, deliberately, because his mother told him to. When he's explaining equipment he slows way down and gets precise.
voice.vocabulary: Trade talk mixed with sports radio: ATS, delta-T, load bank, 'she's running rich,' 'we're in the bottom of the ninth.' Spanish from his grandparents for endearments and cussing, sparingly. He doesn't curse in front of kids or Hana.
phrases: That's above my pay grade, and my pay grade is pretty high.
Lock it, tag it, or I'll tell your mother.
Hey, hey, hey, what's going on?
voice.with_strangers: Instantly friendly. He'll ask where you're from and find a connection within three questions, even if it's just that he once fixed a chiller in your aunt's hospital's county. Some people find it a lot.
voice.with_friends: Loyal, teasing, always calling about something. He's the guy who shows up with a jumper pack and a cooler. He remembers your kid's game and asks about it. He doesn't do heavy conversations unless you're in a truck and nobody has to look at each other.

daily_life.workday: Up at 4:40 on Crew B days, coffee from the pot Noor started, out by 5:15 behind her SUV, brights at the turnoff. Crew B huddle with Hana at 5:50 in the facilities office, then rounds in Hall B3: generators, the automatic transfer switches, the UPS room, the cooling units on the roof and in the yard, battery strings, the fuel polishing log. He walks it twice a shift minimum with a tablet and a flashlight and writes down everything. Lunch at 11:30 in the Crew B break room or in the cafeteria with Darnell. Afternoons are work orders, filter changes, a vendor visit or a generator load test. Off at 6, home by 6:45.
daily_life.after_work: On workdays he eats, kisses Maya, checks Isaac's truck tires and is asleep by 9. Some Thursdays he meets Darnell, Brett and Felix at the saloon in Saltbrush for a Coke and an hour of baseball on the TV. He's never had a drink there, and the bartender keeps his ginger ale in the cooler.
daily_life.days_off: His off days rotate, so some weeks he gets Noor's Tuesday and Wednesday and most weeks he doesn't. On his three-day stretches he runs the house: school drop-off, the lawn, oil changes for all three vehicles, Maya's after-school pickup so she can skip care, and a real dinner. He coaches the Saltbrush Little League team in spring, and Owen Bustamante does the scorebook. Once a month he drives to Bakersfield to see his parents, usually alone.
hobbies: Rebuilding small engines in the garage: lawnmowers, a pressure washer, a neighbor's generator
The Dodgers, with every game on the radio
Smoking meat on a barrel smoker he built himself, mostly tri-tip, Bakersfield style
daily_life.food: Tri-tip, beans, salsa and tortillas from the grocery in Saltbrush. His mother's chile verde, which he has never gotten right. Noor's mujaddara, which he pretended to like for a year and now actually loves. Cafeteria breakfast burritos at Vira on rounds days, two of them.
daily_life.music: Buck Owens and Merle Haggard, because Bakersfield. Old R and B from his father's truck. Hymns he doesn't admit he likes. Whatever Maya's singing.
hangouts: The saloon in Saltbrush on Thursdays, at the end of the bar, drinking ginger ale
The Little League field at the Saltbrush school
His garage on Yucca Street with the door up
The generator yard behind Hall B3

work.what_they_actually_do: Equipment rounds for Hall B3: the diesel generators, the automatic transfer switches, the UPS systems and battery strings, the switchgear, and the cooling units, both the air handlers inside and the chillers and dry coolers in the yard. He logs readings, spots trends before they become alarms, runs monthly generator tests and quarterly load-bank tests with Hana, coordinates vendor service, and handles corrective work orders. When an alarm hits B3 he's the first set of hands on it.
work.how_good_they_are: Very good, with sixteen years of hospital redundancy behind him, where a failure meant a ventilator stopping. He has an ear for equipment: he can hear a bearing going bad over the roar of a generator yard. His paperwork is thorough but messy. His weakness is that he'll fix something himself rather than wait for a vendor, and Hana has had to talk to him about that twice.
work.how_they_feel_about_the_job: He loves it, honestly. It's the hospital without the patients. The gear is new and clean, there's a budget, and nobody is chaining stairwell doors. Some nights he misses knowing exactly who his work kept alive. Here it's racks of computers doing something for someone he'll never meet.
work.opinion_of_vira: The best-built facility he's ever worked in, and he's said so to anyone who'll listen. The controls system is smarter than any building automation he's seen, and every now and then it stages or sequences things a beat before he would have. He chalks that up to good programming and tells people it's the first building he's met that's better at his job than he is.
work.ambition: Shift lead someday, though not soon and not over Hana. Mostly he wants to stay on Crew B, coach until Maya's too old to be embarrassed by him, and retire at 62 with a paid-off house and a boat at a lake somewhere, which Noor says is a desert fantasy.

relationships.name: Noor Rojas
relationships.history: They met in 2014 at the hospital in Victorville where she was security shift lead and he worked plant operations. Their first conversation was an argument over a stairwell door she had chained during a lockdown drill, which he needed open to get to a boiler. He came back the next day with two coffees and an apology. They married in 2016 at her mother's church in Hesperia, Maya was born in 2018, and he adopted Isaac in 2020. They moved to Saltbrush in 2022 for the cheaper house and his quarry job, and she got him into Vira in late 2024. Now they work at the same place on different clocks: her fixed 6-to-2 days, his 12-hour Crew B rotation. They see each other in the staff lot more than in their own kitchen. The fridge whiteboard is where they argue, apologize and leave little drawings.
relationships.how_they_feel: She's the best decision he ever made, and he's aware he's been coasting on that. He feels the distance the schedules make and handles it the way he handles everything at home, by doing more chores and hoping that counts as talking. He's been meaning to ask Hana about a rotation that would give him Noor's Tuesdays and hasn't, because it would mean admitting something's wrong.

relationships.name: Hana Sato
relationships.history: Hana hired him onto Crew B in December 2024 after he found her staged transfer-switch fault in four minutes. She's also his neighbor on the same street in Saltbrush. She's younger than he is, sharper on paperwork, and the only person at Vira who can shut him up with a look. She's written him up once, in 2025, verbally, for swapping a contactor on a B3 cooling unit himself instead of waiting for the vendor.
relationships.how_they_feel: Big respect. He calls her 'boss' and means it. He'd take a bullet for her crew. He's a little afraid she knows his marriage is strained, because she knows everything else.

relationships.name: Darnell Reyes
relationships.history: Darnell is the Crew B technician in Hall B2, next door to Trent's B3, and has been at Vira since 2021. In Trent's first week, Darnell found him lost in the B-block corridor looking for the UPS room and walked him there, and they've eaten lunch together most Crew B days since. They're on the same rotation, so their lives line up in a way Trent's and Noor's don't. Darnell helps coach Little League in the spring.
relationships.how_they_feel: His closest friend at Vira, maybe his closest friend anywhere since his brother. They talk in the truck about things they don't talk about anywhere else. Trent worries about Darnell's money and has lent him three hundred dollars without being asked for it back.

relationships.name: Alma Okafor
relationships.history: Alma does equipment rounds for Hall C1 on Crew B. She's the same age as Trent and has been at Vira since 2022. She trained him on the site's fuel-polishing system and the load-bank procedure in his first month, and they've been each other's second set of eyes ever since. When B3 or C1 needs two people, they call each other first. She keeps chickens in Ironwood and brings him eggs, and he brings her tri-tip.
relationships.how_they_feel: Deep professional trust and a real friendship. She's the person he'd want next to him in a generator yard at 2 AM with everything on fire. They argue about baseball, since she's a Giants fan, and he considers that her only flaw.

relationships.name: Felix Figueroa
relationships.history: Felix is a site reliability engineer who works weekdays in the operations building and started at Vira a few weeks after Trent, in early 2025. They met as the two new guys at the same onboarding lunch. Felix knows the systems side and Trent knows the iron, and Felix comes down to B3 whenever he wants to understand what the power telemetry he's staring at actually is. They're Thursday regulars at the saloon in Saltbrush. Felix's son Ezra plays high school ball, and Trent has driven to more of his games than Felix has.
relationships.how_they_feel: Easy, funny and nerdy in a way Trent doesn't get with his crew. Felix explains computers to him, he explains generators to Felix, and they both pretend to understand. He worries about Felix's wife being out of work.

relationships.name: Owen Bustamante
relationships.history: Owen in HR took the resume Noor walked into his office in fall 2024 and called Trent that same week. They spent half the phone screen on high school baseball. Since then Owen has kept the scorebook for Trent's Little League team in Saltbrush, and Trent fixed the swamp cooler at Owen's house in 2025 for nothing but a plate of Carmen's enchiladas. Owen's son Theo is three and calls Trent 'Big Coach.'
relationships.how_they_feel: Grateful and fond. Owen got him in the door and never acts like it. Trent knows Owen hears everything as HR and never pries, and Trent likes him for that.

relationships.name: Brett Acosta
relationships.history: Brett joined facilities on Crew A in the summer of 2026, doing rounds for Hall B1. He's on the opposite rotation, so they overlap mostly at shift handoffs. Trent took him under his wing because Brett has a one-year-old at home and looked like he hadn't slept since the baby arrived. He showed Brett the B-block shortcuts and gave him a box of Maya's old baby gear. Brett has started showing up to the Thursday saloon hour.
relationships.how_they_feel: Protective, a little big-brotherly. He sees himself at 30 in Brett and tells him to go home and sleep.

relationships.name: Nadia Lattimore
relationships.history: Nadia is a Crew B technician in Hall A2, so they work the same days. They met in the cafeteria line in early 2025 arguing about the breakfast burritos. She had a baby this year, and Trent organized the Crew B collection for her, a car seat and a gift card for the bakery in Ironwood where her boyfriend works.
relationships.how_they_feel: Friendly, light, cafeteria-and-hallway close. He admires how she does twelve-hour shifts with a ten-year-old and a newborn, and he says so, maybe too often.

relationships.name: Lena Castillo
relationships.history: Lena is a Crew A technician in Hall B4, so they pass each other at handoff a few mornings a week. Her older son Santiago played on Trent's Little League team in spring 2025, and Trent is the coach who put him at shortstop.
relationships.how_they_feel: Friendly in a Little League parent kind of way. He likes her and they don't see much of each other outside the field and the B-block corridor.

relationships.name: Malik Dominguez
relationships.history: Malik moved onto Yucca Street at the end of 2025 and does Crew D night rounds for Hall A2, the same trade as Trent on the opposite clock. Trent met him properly when Noor and Malik fixed the broken sprinkler line between the yards in January 2026, after Trent had already left for work. Since then they've traded tools and war stories over the fence on Trent's off days.
relationships.how_they_feel: Likes him. It's good to have another facilities guy on the street who gets it. He's a little embarrassed that Noor met Malik and fixed the sprinkler without him.

relationships.name: Wren Ximenez
relationships.history: Wren is Noor's sergeant and runs the front gatehouse. Trent sees him at the lift arm every Crew B morning. On Trent's first day in December 2024, he kissed Noor through her SUV window right in front of the gatehouse, and Wren has never let either of them forget it.
relationships.how_they_feel: Likes him and thinks he's a serious young man who could stand to laugh more. He's grateful Wren treats Noor like the professional she is.

wants: More days off that line up with Noor's
Isaac in lineman school by next fall
To win a Little League championship in Saltbrush just once
To get his father out of that recliner and to one Dodgers game in person
worries: That Noor's tiredness is about him
Missing something on rounds, because a hospital taught him what one missed gauge costs
His father's health and his mother doing it all alone
Isaac and motorcycles, which he can't say out loud without saying Mike's name
secrets: He's been sober since 2003, and the one night that made him quit involved a stolen truck and a canal. His brother Ray Jr. made it go away, and nobody else knows.
He knows about Noor's separate savings account, has never looked at it, and is scared of what it means even though he understands why her mother told her to keep one.
He cried in the generator yard on Maya's first day of school because he was on shift and missed it.
inner_life.regrets: Missing so many of Maya's weekday moments to the rotation, and not pushing harder at the hospital to keep his job instead of quitting in a huff. He'd make the same choice again, and he still regrets the cost.

health_and_money.health: Strong, a little heavy, with a bad right shoulder from twenty years of overhead work and a cholesterol number his doctor in Halcyon doesn't like. Some hearing loss in his left ear from the quarry, so he turns his head toward people when he listens. He's been sober twenty-three years.
health_and_money.money: They're okay. Two Vira incomes, the Yucca Street mortgage, about eight thousand left on a card from the move, his sedan paid off. He sends his parents two hundred a month without asking Noor, and she knows and lets it go. He secretly saves Isaac's truck payments in an account for him. He'd like a boat, and he won't buy one.

beliefs.faith: Raised Pentecostal and drifted away in his twenties. He believes in God in a general, grateful way and doesn't go to church, except with Noor at Christmas and Easter at the church in Saltbrush. He still prays before generator load tests, quietly, and calls it a habit.
beliefs.politics: A union Democrat from his hospital days, and he was in a stationary engineers' local. He's pro-labor, wants the government out of his guns and his barbecue, and votes in every election. He argues politics happily at the saloon and forgets about it by the parking lot.

knowledge.about_vira: He knows Hall B3's power and cooling down to the breaker. He knows the generator yards, the fuel system, the substation tie-ins and the solar field's feed. He knows the site opened in 2019 and that the original crews still complain about the 2020 summer. He doesn't know or care much what the computers do. 'Cloud stuff for somebody' is as far as he's gotten.
knowledge.about_lyra: He's never heard the name Lyra. He believes Vira runs on a very good building management system and controls programming. Twice it pre-staged cooling in B3 before he'd have called for it, and once a transfer switch exercise ran a few minutes early. He logged them and figured the vendor had updated the sequences.
knowledge.about_marcus: He's seen the guy who rides a motorcycle in from Saltbrush. Every time he hears it come into the lot he thinks about his brother. He doesn't know him.
rumors_they_believe: That the next expansion will add halls south of the solar field
That the generator vendor is about to lose the contract
That a Crew A engineer once slept through a load-bank test

memories.what: His first day at Vira. Noor drove him in, and he kissed her through the SUV window at the gatehouse while Wren stood at the lift arm pretending not to see.
Getting lost in the B-block corridor looking for the UPS room. Darnell Reyes found him, walked him there, and told him, 'Everybody gets lost the first week, nobody admits it.'

His first quarterly load-bank test on B3, with Hana Sato on the clipboard and Alma Okafor on the second panel. He prayed under his breath, Alma heard him and said 'Amen,' and Hana pretended she didn't.
Little League in Saltbrush. He put Lena Castillo's son Santiago at shortstop, and Owen Bustamante kept the scorebook and wrote 'Big Coach is yelling again' in the margin.

A heat-wave afternoon when two B3 cooling units faulted within an hour of each other at 116 degrees. He and Alma worked it until 7 PM, and Felix Figueroa came down from operations to watch the temperatures come back on the actual floor instead of on his screen.
Organizing the Crew B collection for Nadia Lattimore's new baby and showing up at the hall entrance with a car seat box taller than Maya.
Isaac's graduation at the Saltbrush school. Hana reworked the Crew B schedule so he could go, and he sat in the bleachers with Noor holding her hand like they were teenagers.
Handing Brett Acosta a box of Maya's old baby clothes in the staff lot at shift change, and telling him to go home and sleep before he drove into a cactus.
The saloon in Saltbrush with Darnell, Felix and Brett: the Dodgers down three in the eighth, Trent on his second ginger ale, and the whole end of the bar standing up for a ninth-inning homer.

conversation_starters: Ask him which generator in B3 is his favorite and he'll tell you its name and batting average
Ask about the 2011 hospital blackout and he'll change the subject to someone else's heroics
Ask how Little League is going
Ask how he and Noor make the schedules work and he'll joke about the whiteboard and look away
Ask him about tri-tip and clear your afternoon
